sections.h2: Which Lake County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Two county offices split the work. The Lake County Auditor values every parcel and keeps the tax list, and the Lake County Treasurer sends out the bills and collects. The Auditor's about page counts more than 111,000 parcels in the county and says Ohio law calls for a general reappraisal every six years with an update every three years. The same page states that the Auditor does not raise or lower taxes: rates come from levies voters approve.

The Auditor's real estate staff can be reached at (440) 350-2532 for owner address changes and credit questions. The Treasurer's billing line is (440) 350-2516, and the delinquent tax division takes calls at 440-350-2473. The Treasurer's office is open 8:00 to 4:30 on weekdays at 105 Main Street, Painesville, and the county's tax lookup for any parcel sits on the Auditor's real property search.

sections.h2: When are Lake County real estate taxes due?
sections.html:
Ohio bills real estate tax in two halves. The Lake County Treasurer's page lists the dates by the year the tax is payable, and the first set below has already passed.

Lake County real estate tax due dates as listed on the Treasurer's welcome page
Tax year and payable yearFirst halfSecond half
2025 tax, payable 2026Wednesday, February 25, 2026Wednesday, August 5, 2026
2026 tax, payable 2027Wednesday, February 24, 2027Wednesday, July 21, 2027

A bill paid late draws a 10 percent penalty under the Ohio Revised Code, and interest is charged twice a year on certified unpaid balances. A postmark from the United States Postal Service counts as timely. Under section 323.13 of the Revised Code, as the Treasurer quotes it, the owner is responsible for the tax even if a bill never arrives, and the Treasurer asks owners to call if nothing has come by February 1 or July 1. The Auditor's FAQ says bills generally go out in mid-January and mid-June, with payment due roughly 20 to 30 days later. The Treasurer also lists dates for manufactured homes, which differ from the real estate dates.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Lake County property value?
sections.html:
Only the value can be appealed, because the rate is set by levies. The Board of Revision accepts complaints from January 1 through March 31 of each year on form DTE 1, and the Treasurer's notices list the next filing period as opening January 1, 2027.

  • The Board has three members: the Auditor, the Treasurer and the President of the County Commissioners.
  • Evidence goes in with the complaint, or at least 5 days before the hearing.
  • Typical residential hearings last about 15 minutes, and a decision notice comes in roughly 2 to 3 weeks.
  • Useful evidence includes a recent arm's length sale, a listing or purchase agreement, an appraisal as of the January 1 lien date, photos of damage and a market analysis from a real estate professional.
  • The Board will not weigh the percentage rise in your tax bill or the difference between your value and a neighbor's.

If you disagree with the decision, you can appeal to the Ohio Board of Tax Appeals on form DTE 4 within 30 days of the notice mailing, or to the Lake County Court of Common Pleas. If an appraisal is your evidence, the appraiser must appear to testify.

sections.h2: What tax relief applies in Lake County after the 2025 reform bills?
sections.html:
The Treasurer's notice says five property tax reform bills, Ohio House Bills 186, 335, 124, 129 and 309, were signed on December 19, 2025, with adjustments phased in over three years. The first affects the July 2026 bill, where applicable credits or reductions are printed. Residential, agricultural and most business properties qualify without an application, and the Treasurer advises contacting your mortgage company once the credit shows so the escrow payment can be adjusted.

The notice also says the homestead credit is doubled for 2026 tax payable in 2027, while the owner occupancy credit is not. For the details, call the Auditor's real estate desk at 440-350-2532. The Auditor's about page describes the homestead exemption as means tested for new participants, so ask for the current household income limit before you apply.

sections.h2: How are Lake County property taxes handled when a house sells?
sections.html:
An ordinary sale settles the current year's tax at closing, usually through a title company. The county's pro-rating page is written for sheriff sales: after a sale is confirmed, the Treasurer gives the total due at that time and prorates the following year's tax from the current year's full-year real estate tax plus long-term assessments such as lighting or storm water. The proration starts 90 days after the sheriff sale, and requests go to the Treasurer by email. The figure is an estimate, and the Treasurer is not responsible for later garbage bills, levy changes or value changes.

The conveyance fee is a separate item at the Auditor. The Auditor's FAQ puts it at $4.00 for every $1,000 of the purchase price plus $0.50 per parcel, and section 319.202 puts it on the seller. Anyone enrolled in the Treasurer's automatic payment plan should know that a final bill is not paid through that plan, so the seller's closing agent has to settle it.

sections.h2: What if Lake County property tax is behind?
sections.html:
The Treasurer's pages describe several routes before and after delinquency:

  • A delinquent payment plan for primary residences and manufactured homes runs two years, with a down payment equal to half a year's tax and an appointment required.
  • A tax lien sale can include a property with delinquency in three billing cycles after multiple notices and newspaper publication, and the page says it is not a sale of the property. An administrative fee of $100.00 applies with the first notice and $200.00 on the sale date, and the sale is generally held every fall.
  • The payment plan page says lien sales can lead to 18 percent interest and added fees.
  • The Treasurer holds the first and best lien on real property. A lien purchaser can ask for foreclosure if the lien is not repaid or on a plan within 18 months, and the county prosecutor can also file in the Treasurer's name, which may lead to a sheriff sale.

A seller who owes back tax can still sell if the payoff clears at closing, so ask the delinquent tax division for a written payoff figure before signing a contract.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about Lake County?
sections.html:
Lake County is the smallest Ohio county by land area, at 227 square miles, yet it has a total area of 979 square miles because the county owns the lake bed under its 31 mile shoreline. The Census Bureau estimates 232,217 residents for July 2025 and 107,571 housing units. The owner-occupied rate is 75.8 percent, the median owner-occupied home is valued at $214,100 and median selected owner costs with a mortgage are $1,500 a month.

The Auditor's about page lists the taxing units that share each bill: five townships, nine villages, nine cities, ten school districts and eight library systems. Painesville is the county seat and Mentor is the largest city, so a parcel's total rate depends on which of those districts it falls in.

faqs.q: When are Lake County real estate taxes due for 2026 tax payable in 2027?
faqs.a: The Treasurer lists February 24, 2027 for the first half and July 21, 2027 for the second half of 2026 tax payable in 2027. The last 2025 tax payment was due August 5, 2026.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Lake County property tax bill?
faqs.a: You can appeal only the property's value, since levies set the rate. File form DTE 1 with the Board of Revision between January 1 and March 31. The Auditor's page says the Board does not hear complaints about taxes.

faqs.q: What is the Lake County conveyance fee when I sell?
faqs.a: The Auditor's FAQ states $4.00 per $1,000 of the purchase price and $0.50 per parcel. The state share is $1.00 per $1,000 and the county share is $3.00, adopted by resolution on March 26, 1990.

faqs.q: What penalty applies to late Lake County property tax?
faqs.a: A 10 percent penalty applies under the Ohio Revised Code, and interest is charged twice yearly on certified unpaid balances. Not receiving a bill does not remove the penalty, according to section 323.13. A payment plan can stop the penalties from growing.

faqs.q: Does Lake County let a homeowner with delinquent taxes set up a payment plan?
faqs.a: Yes. The Treasurer offers a two year plan for primary residences and manufactured homes, with an appointment and a down payment of half a year's tax. Call 440-350-2473 to arrange one.
